# The habit: the run, the receipt, a moment and the measure

How many weeks in a row a person has been on time, with one late week forgiven; what the check-in’s last screen says once the week’s are all in; when a check-in says a goal reached its target or came back on track; and how many of a set’s goals were checked in before the review without being asked.

## The rule

The habit Faro most wants is checking in before the review without being asked. This page is the part a person sees about themselves; nothing here compares people, and a run is only ever shown to its owner.

**Why it has no switch.** The habit is core, not a module: the run counts the status rules' own check-ins by week, and the receipt and the moment are the check-in's last screen, so there is nothing separate to turn off. Its words follow the reviews switch through dueWords (RS1: with Reviews off, or no review held that day, the due day is a plain deadline), and it reads no module's records.

**The run** (`onTimeStreak`). A week is *on time* when the person had something due in it and every goal they own that was due was checked in by them on or before the week's review day (`inByDueDay`: the day the check-in was posted, on the reader's own clock, the clock Home's "due today" is read on, so Home, the receipt and the run name one due day; reviews have a day and no hour), in that week: a week added later (backfilled) is never on time, and a removed check-in doesn't count. A goal is due for the person from its first due week, or from the week after someone else last checked it in (a goal taken over counts only from when it was theirs), until the week it was called Done (Done goals leave the run as they leave the week's count). Walk back from the latest finished week (this week counts once every goal is checked in; otherwise start from last week), counting on-time weeks. A week that is not on time is **forgiven** when each of the 4 weeks before it in which the person had something due was on time: it isn't counted, and the walk goes on. A week not on time and not forgiven ends the walk, and so does a week with nothing due. "Checked in this week, but late" is a late week like any other. A forgiven week is *missed* when a goal due in it has no check-in of theirs posted in its week, and *late* otherwise. `forgivenIn` gives the latest forgiven week inside the run, or none. The forgiving run is the default (CF4); a workspace setting to make it strict or hide it comes with CF2's `streak` column, which isn't built: until then every workspace forgives.

**The receipt** (`receiptText`, from `receiptFacts`), once every one of the person's check-ins for the week is in. It reads their goals this week, how many of them were first checked in after the due day, and the deadline in dueWords' words (`dueWords` with `heldOnDueDay` for the person: "before {Thursday}’s review" only while Reviews is on and a live review they are in is held that day; otherwise "by {Thursday}", and Faro never calls a deadline a review), the run, the forgiven week and the next due day:

- all in by the due day: "{Your check-in is | Both of your check-ins are | All {n} of your check-ins are} in before {Thursday}’s review." (in no review held that day, or with Reviews off, "… in by {Thursday}.": the deadline is dueWords', [rule RS1](../../modules/reviews/rules.md)), then, from a run of 2, "That is {k} weeks in a row."; and on the first receipt after a forgiven week (it is last week), "Week {w} came in late; one late week doesn’t break a run.", or, when nothing of theirs came in that week, "Week {w} was missed; one missed week doesn’t break a run.";
- some after: "{…} in. {It | One | Both | All of them | {m}} came after {Thursday}’s review." (or "came after {Thursday}.") then "The next {is | are} due by {Thursday 19 Nov}." No run is mentioned, and none is said to be lost.

Never said: "streak lost", "broken", a nought, a count of late weeks, an exclamation mark. A person is never told that an ask came before their check-in. Home's quiet line says the same two sentences on the day the week is completed ([Home](home.md)), and `get_my_work` gives them as `weekReceipt`.

**A moment** (`moment`, for the goal's earlier check-ins and this one). *Reached*: a number goal's value meets its target in the goal's direction (at or above it when the target is above the start, at or below it otherwise) and the latest check-in of the week before did not. *Back*: the status is On track, the week before's was At risk or Off track, and the goal had been behind (At risk or Off track) for 2 weeks or more in a row. Reached wins over back; one per check-in. Neither fires on a correction, a second check-in in the same week, a backfilled week or an import. The receipt shows one panel above the week's lines: the check-in's own status, its shape and word, "{Goal} reached its target" and "{value}, against a target of {target}, in week {w} of {weeks}. It started the year at {start}." with **Copy the share image** (the image carries that same status); or "{Goal} is back on track" and "{value}, after {k} weeks behind plan.". The page's own **View the goal** goes to the goal. History's row for that check-in adds "Reached its target" or "Back on track" in small capitals, in the status's colour, with no capsule. `post_check_in` answers with the same `moment`. No animation beyond the receipt's own, no confetti, no banner on anyone else's screen.

**The measure** is the share of goals checked in before the review without a nudge; Faro's only nudge is an ask for an update. *A check-in's standing* (`checkInStanding`, rule 1), for a goal due that week (`dueIn`: not stopped or proposed, first due by then, not done before it): `none` when no check-in counts for the week; `after` when the first was posted after the end of the due day (the week's review day); `asked` when it was in by then and an ask for an update on the goal was open when it was posted (asked before it, and answered at or after it, or still open); `unasked` otherwise. A question, a comment or a review's carried action is not a nudge, and a correction doesn't change a week's standing. *The counts* (`habit`, rule 2) over a set of goals: `due`, `unasked`, `asked`, `after`, `none`, and `inTime` = unasked + asked; the measure is unasked / due. *The row of weeks* (`habitWeeks`): the last 8 weeks up to the review's week once its due day has passed (the week before, until then), each `all` ("All in": every goal due was in by the due day), `some` ("{k} after": k came after or not at all), `none` ("None in") or `nothing-due` ("Nothing due"), drawn as a filled, half-filled or open square, or no mark: squares, because a circle is a goal's status.

**A leader's Home** (`habitCell`, HB3). Beside [how the week's check-ins stand](home-leader.md), for the same viewer and the same set, one more cell: rule 2's measure for this week. "Before the review, without being asked" ("On time, without being asked" unless a review is held on the due day for these goals, RS1); "{u} of {n} goals · {p}%", the percentage only from `PERCENT_FROM` (20) goals due, `p` being `u / n` rounded; before the due day, "So far: {u} of {n} goals". Under it, "Week {w-1}: {p}%" when last week had a percentage, and "By week" (`byWeekTo`): the review covering most of the set's goals due this week, or the set in Goals when none covers any. Rule 4 holds: fewer than three owners among the goals due, no cell. Nothing due, no cell.

**Before this review** (`beforeReview`, `beforeReviewText`), at the top of a review's page for the goals it walks (for its session's week, or this week while the session's week is still to come; the counts are judged against the workspace's due day, so a review held on any other day is headed "Week {w}, due by {Thu 19 Nov}" and worded as the deadline, never "before it"), and on a team's page for the team's goals headed "Before this week’s review": "{a} of {n} goals were checked in before it, {u} without being asked" ("…, all without being asked" when a is u; "All {n} goals were checked in before it, without anyone asking" when every one was, unasked; "None of the {n} goals was checked in before it."); before the due day, "{a} of {n} goals are checked in so far." Under it, each only when not nought, "{k} came in after an ask" (Goals `checkedin=asked`) and "{m} have no check-in for week {w} yet" (`checkedin=no`), each with the set's own parameter (`inreview=` or `team=`) and worst first, and only for this week (what `checkedin=` reads); then the row of weeks and "“All in” means every goal due that week was checked in before the review. Weeks, not people: nobody is named here." With Reviews switched off there is no review's page. A team's page says "review" only when Reviews is on and a review is held on the due day with one of the team's goals' owners in it (`heldForGoals`); otherwise, Reviews on or off, it heads the panel "Week {w}, due by {Thursday 12 Nov}", says "checked in on time" where it says "before it", and "by its {Thursday}" under the row of weeks (dueWords' words, Reviews switch spec 2.1; the habit never imports reviews). `get_review` gives the same as `beforeThisReview`.

**Never a person** (`habitShown`, rule 4): a set whose goals due that week have fewer than 3 owners shows no panel, row or count, unless the viewer owns all of them. No function here takes or returns a person, and nothing here sorts, compares or ranks people or teams by their share, sets a target for it, or makes a status of it.

| Due Thursday 12 Nov: checked in Tuesday, no ask; asked for an update Wednesday and checked in Wednesday evening; a question Tuesday, checked in Wednesday; checked in Friday; no check-in. | `unasked, asked, unasked, after, none` |

| A team’s goals with two owners, seen by someone else; then by their one owner; then four owners. | `hidden, shown, shown` |
| The same 20 h, backfilled. | `none` |

- [src/domain/review.ts](../../../src/domain/review.ts): `heldOnDueDay`
- [src/domain/habit.ts](../../../src/domain/habit.ts): `moment`, `momentText`, `BACK_AFTER`, `MOMENT_RESULT`, `habit`, `habitWeeks`, `weekWords`, `habitShown`, `MIN_OWNERS`, `beforeReviewText`, `beforeReview`, `habitCell`, `PERCENT_FROM`, `byWeekTo`

## Requirements

- `HABIT-RECEIPT`: Once a person's check-ins for the week are all in, the receipt says whether they were in before the deadline ("All 4 of your check-ins are in for week 46, before Thursday’s deadline."; the due day is called a review only for someone in a review held that day) and the run of weeks in a row on time, from two; or how many came in after it and when the next are due, with no run. One late week is forgiven when the four weeks before it were on time, and said once ("Week 45 came in late; one late week doesn’t break a run."). Never "lost", "broken", a nought or an exclamation mark. Home's quiet line says the same two sentences on the day the week is completed.
- `HABIT-MOMENT`: A check-in that reaches a goal's target, or brings it back on track after two weeks or more behind, shows one quiet panel on its receipt (the status's shape and word, what happened in one line, "Copy the share image" for a target reached) and its row in the goal's History says "Reached its target" or "Back on track" in small capitals. Never on a correction, a backfilled week or an import; no animation, confetti or banner on anyone else's screen.
- `HABIT-MEASURE`: A review's page says how many of its goals were checked in before it, and how many without being asked (Faro's only nudge is an ask for an update), with links that open exactly the goals that came in after an ask and those with no check-in yet, and a row of the last 8 weeks (All in, {k} after, None in, Nothing due) drawn as squares with words. A team's page shows the same for its goals.
- `HABIT-NEVER-A-PERSON`: The measure is about weeks and goals, never people: no person is named, listed, counted or sorted in it, no team is ranked by it, and a set whose goals have fewer than three owners shows none of it, unless the viewer owns them all.
